entry.title: RICPE correction: Aweswell’s procedural representation and good-faith third-party exposure
entry.summary: Visible correction of the earlier version: the 26 May 2020 record establishes the change in Aweswell’s procedural representation in Concurso 36/2012, not a global termination. Any later effect on residual trust, confidentiality or assistance remains an allegation requiring proof. Unnecessary private economic detail is removed and the institutional formulation is now potential instrumentalisation of good-faith third parties, asymmetric socialisation of risk and economic and institutional anchoring, without attributing knowledge or complicity to exposed third parties. The dossier adds an audience map and a request for a reasoned correction-and-notification decision.

entry.title: RICPE: 2021 alert, Sony Ganwani, residual assistance and alleged-harm perimeter
entry.summary: A controlled public chronology covers the 2019 functional connection with Sony; Aweswell’s specific procedural change of counsel in Concurso 36/2012 on 26 May 2020; the 8 March 2021 alert; metadata for the 17 March voice note; and Enrique Guerra’s RICPE certificate filed in the proceeding on 21 July. The 2021 message could not have caused the earlier procedural change. Gil makes the narrower allegation that Íñigo referred to “our friend Sony” and presented himself as a messenger, and that this may have affected residual channels of trust, confidentiality or assistance. No RICPE mandate, leak or caused outcome is asserted. There is no retrospective Law 2/2023 label; any later act requires separate proof under Articles 36.2 and 63.

entry.title: Lender of Record: credit chain, financial package and LPB concurso perimeter
entry.summary: New page separating the mortgage-credit chain from the disputed Bankia/CaixaBank financial package and adding a site-wide qualification against treating the limited LPB concurso as authority over the whole hotel or later operation.

entry.title: New series: Inparsa, Meeting Point and Canary Islands hotel valuation
entry.summary: Three bilingual analyses distinguish the criminal-law threshold in Inparsa/Hoteles Beatriz, the successive attribution of two judicial names in Meeting Point 357/2024 and the non-interchangeable figures in the Anfi, Taurito and Inparsa transactions. Sun Park links are limited to replicable questions about debt, value, control, knowledge and remedy; professional or institutional proximity is not presented as evidence of guilt.

entry.title: Eleven institutional records and complete legal/privacy notice published
entry.summary: Eleven bilingual, source-controlled records are live: eight concerning Ministerio Fiscal, Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ), Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV), Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Servicio Nacional de Coordinación Antifraude (SNCA), Gobierno de Canarias, Ayuntamiento de Yaiza and Cabildo de Lanzarote; and three concerning the separate public-law professional corporations Ilustre Colegio de Abogados de Las Palmas (ICALPA), Colegio Oficial de Arquitectos de Gran Canaria (COAGC) and Colegio Oficial de Arquitectos de Lanzarote (COALZ). ICALPA DIP 79/2026 and DIP 80/2026 are preliminary-information proceedings, not breach findings; COAGC references do not prove that it visaed or approved the project; and COALZ RE 26/008230 proves receipt, not a merits decision. A visado proves no ownership, promoter authority, planning legality or criminal liability. The complete legal/privacy notice identifies Gil Marer as responsible editor and publishes evidence, correction, proceedings and privacy protocols.

entry.title: Writer pack: judicial control, Inparsa and the Sun Park allegation
entry.summary: A new bilingual framework and PDF pack examine what separates an adverse commercial ruling from possible prevaricación. Inparsa is used only as a methodological comparator, never as evidence against the Sun Park judge. The page separates facts, allegations, disputes and gaps; tests Penal Code articles 446 to 449 individually; identifies José Carlos González Vázquez as a natural reader because of his public analyses without implying knowledge, representation or endorsement; and records that no primary TSJC order or later public outcome was located.

entry.title: Legal Notebook: Inparsa/Hoteles Beatriz and Santana Cazorla/Anfi/Lopesan
entry.summary: A bilingual, source-led legal desk opens with two separate Canary Islands matters involving hotel assets, valuation, competition and changes of control. Each case distinguishes decisions, allegations, procedural reports and inference, identifies missing primary records and provides a page-scoped moderated contribution thread.

entry.title: Superseding correction: CEXP, Monterecco/Pink cession and Order 804/2018
entry.summary: Supersedes the earlier formulation: CEXP participation in 2008 was expressly voluntary; 74.90% of the complex approved and 10.01% opposed or reserved. The signed 1 February 2012 cession and Monterecco’s official 159-unit/477-bed perimeter are incorporated; authority and scope are the remaining issues. Order 804/2018 affirmed provisional criminal archive, not a trial finding of Pink’s total abandonment or operator title; the original May 2017 record distinguishes cessation of new commercialisation, guest services, maintenance and later handover.

entry.title: Canonical dossier: Sun Park minutes, actors and authority, 2011–2022
entry.summary: A new bilingual dossier separates Owners’ Community minutes, CEXP minutes and linked non-minutes records; adds the 1 February 2012 CEXP–Monterecco notice, the official 159-unit/477-bed tourism perimeter, the Community request received by Cabildo on 4 June 2014 and the 12 June 2017 meeting; fixes evidential limits and notice to the insolvency administrator; and labels unresolved theories without presenting them as convictions.

entry.title: Canonical dossier: the 7 June 2018 material takeover of Sun Park
entry.summary: New bilingual dossier on the live hotel, the ONA exit proposal, material takeover, guests and staff, the limits of Insolvency 36/2012, the roles of the administrator and judge, and evidence of pilots preceding LPB title in 2022. Atilano Sastre is presented as a direct professional source; the El Corte Inglés Empresas lead remains unnamed.

entry.title: Unitary reverse story: from MYND Yaiza back to origin
entry.summary: The homepage now connects the 2022–present outcome to 2021 notice, the 2020 RICPE representations, 2018 material control, credit and particular properties, 2016 PwC/Community knowledge, the 2011 matrix minutes and 2008 fragmentation. Every transition requires title, authority, knowledge and a contemporaneous document.

entry.title: 7 June 2018: material takeover of control without a CAM possession order
entry.summary: The direct eyewitness’s judicial statement describes a broken lock, chains, padlocks, replaced cylinders, uniformed access control and continuing exclusion. The 16 April order directed no possession or eviction. In affirming provisional dismissal, the Court recounted the insolvency administrator’s evidence about access control and entry into LPB premises, together with the dispute’s asserted civil nature and shortcomings in title, possession and criminal proof; it neither conferred CAM possessory title nor determined that authority with civil effect.

entry.title: Webinar, OB REM and JSP units: unitary title control
entry.summary: The brochure’s “under study” label does not neutralise the categorical November 2020 webinar claims. The record now also controls the 31 properties separated through the OB REM operation, applies Sun Park Judgment 89/2014 to individual title, and publishes the 61-property JSP/Montelanza, S.L. schedule.

entry.title: Four non-estate units: PwC control and Montelanza, S.L. title chain
entry.summary: A new visual panel covers four private units represented by name in 2016, three by PwC professionals and one by LPB’s then representative. It publishes Gil Marer’s attributed criminal allegation, the property-by-property question, and analysis of Montelanza, S.L.’s conditional deed, 2017 Registry records and CAM attribution in 2018.

entry.title: Complete index: PwC meeting of 11 June 2016
entry.summary: 176 consolidated contextual interventions by FMMM and Juan Carlos Prieto are published with all six attendees, key statements and the 2021–2023 PwC UK–PwC Spain notice trail. Gil Marer’s normalisation or whitewashing allegation is separated from proved facts and outstanding internal evidence.

entry.title: Dedicated dossier: instrumentalisation of the Community
entry.summary: A new bilingual page covers the Community authority chain, Pamanil and Pamalexsha, the PropCo/OpCo structure, the PwC/Landwell engagement and the transcript of the recorded 2016 meeting. Carlos Saavedra’s public chronology is linked with express evidential limits.

entry.title: 2011 as documentary ground zero and 22 June as the matrix minutes
entry.summary: The reconstruction separates the 2008 collective operating structure from the FMMM era; identifies the 22 June 2011 minutes as the document joining debt, voting exclusion, Pamanil, custody and litigation; follows the chain through 2022; publishes Gil Marer and Monterecco’s then representative’s perspective correction; and distinguishes the 2008 asset transfer from the 2011 purchase of LPB shares from Multimatrix.

entry.title: “The Community” no longer operates as a shortcut to authority
entry.summary: New visual stop and documentary matrix: the label Community, president or administrator does not prove appointment, resolution, mandate, unit scope or verification. The 10 March and 7 April Cabildo records and the 18 June 2026 communication are separated by what each establishes and does not establish.

entry.title: 2021 prosecution route: referral of the file containing the RIC allegations documented
entry.summary: The LexNET receipt identifies the website, webinar and RIC annexes. The 12 and 22 March 2021 orders document notification and subsequent referral of the proceedings to the Public Prosecutor. The individual prosecutor and merits assessment remain undocumented.

entry.title: 2021 alert: substance, recipients and established receipt
entry.summary: New visual map of the 2021 sequence: CNMV and AEAT received direct filings; the insolvency case received, served and placed the chronology before the judge; the administrator and personated parties were notified; the 12 and 22 March orders document notification and referral to the Public Prosecutor; the individual prosecutor and merits assessment remain open. The alert connected title, investors, RIC, the estate, bidding and a circular risk of later validation.

entry.title: Protected report, court filing and the verifiable duty to react
entry.summary: The review distinguishes whistleblower protection from judicial evidential admissibility. The record shows procedural responses but identifies no substantive reconciliation, Article 40.1 LEC referral or Article 82 TRLC supervision report. Non-response may be a procedural breach; it does not prove collusion by itself.

entry.title: Knowledge, decisions and title: the 2021–2022 procedural chain
entry.summary: The chronology documents formal knowledge by the administrator and judge, incompatible orders, clarification, operative certified copies, deed and registration. Gil Marer attributes functional alignment with the CAM-favouring result; no clandestine agreement or offence is stated as proved.

entry.title: Prior notice, surviving Matkator title and current public exposure
entry.summary: CNMV and AEAT were notified in January 2021; the insolvency court received the title and marketing objection in February. CAM/RICPE later acknowledged fragmented ownership, while Matkator’s registered title survives and the operation and public exposure continue.

entry.title: Corrected: Sun Park/MYND materialisation and loans are documented
entry.summary: The audited accounts record Series F and G and EUR 6,573,703.10 materialised and lent to HNT; the BOE records a EUR 3,440,914.20 regional award. The remaining question concerns the truth and sufficiency of the eligibility file.

entry.title: AC and judge journey made static and directly navigable
entry.summary: Both language versions now show a static AC and judge section after the five private actors, with direct navigation and no JavaScript dependency.

entry.title: DIP 2/2026: documented appeal-status error
entry.summary: Court records predating Fiscalía's check already documented appeal RPL 3319/2025. The complete 11 March communication and its contextual explanation are now published.

entry.title: Law 2/2023: formal routing to the Canary Islands Government's internal system
entry.summary: The signed receipt establishes transfer of REGAGE26e00065752755 for treatment under Law 2/2023 and Decree 91/2024, together with outgoing record 681432/2026. A redacted copy is published; it is not a merits decision.

entry.title: Accountability sequence reordered
entry.summary: The five private actors now precede the insolvency administrator and judge to improve causal legibility, without establishing liability or automatic neutrality.
